summary: Implemented culture-independent case profiles and opt-in Unicode whole-word matching for the current managed Search text sources. Sensitive matching retains the exact fast path; insensitive matching uses invariant one-code-unit folding; whole-word matching uses explicit scalar categories, LF record edges and deferred supplementary lookahead while preserving UTF-16 and lossless source-byte coordinates.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search matcher/request/scanner/source implementation, Search tests and related Search documentation were changed. Existing two-argument SQL constructor metadata remains unchanged; no native backend, sibling repository, release, publication, installation or raw-byte search surface was modified.

casePolicy.insensitive: Culture-independent invariant Unicode folding of one UTF-16 code unit at a time; no normalization or one-to-many expansion.
casePolicy.defaults: Sensitive and non-whole-word behavior remain the default; unknown case values fail as invalid request arguments.

wordPolicy.wordScalars: Unicode letters, decimal digits, connector punctuation, non-spacing marks and spacing combining marks.
wordPolicy.boundaries: Only the first and last scalar statuses are compared with neighboring content; underscore and digits are word-like, punctuation and symbols are non-word, and LF is a physical record edge.
wordPolicy.streaming: Whole-word candidates defer one following high surrogate when it ends a reader block, then resolve against the next code unit or successful EOF.

implementation.coordinates: Policy matching retains the existing UTF-16 columns and strict file-backed UTF-8/UTF-16 byte ranges; no source bytes are reconstructed from folded text.

requiredCoverage: Turkish I under tr-TR without current-culture drift, including dotted and dotless variants
German sharp-s and uppercase sharp-s without SS expansion
Greek capital, normal and final sigma invariant matching
Non-ASCII Polish identifiers and supplementary emoji/letter scalar boundaries
A supplementary scalar split across the bounded reader block

gateResults.evidence: The exact owning-repository Release suite exited 0 with 21 projects, 1,400 discovered, 1,366 passed, 0 failed and 34 skips; the focused Search suite exited 0 with 113 passed and 3 expected platform-conditional skips.

The separate ownership review approved the explicit case/word policy, matcher state boundary, coordinate preservation, default compatibility and absence of an advertised native combination; source and artifact hashes plus the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are verified during post-commit finalization.

Focused tests cover Turkish I, German sharp-s, Greek sigma, underscore, digits, combining marks, Polish identifiers, supplementary symbols/letters and invalid case modes, including a supplementary scalar split across reader blocks.
Case and whole-word matching use bounded KMP/ring state plus at most one deferred lookahead code unit; all existing 64-bit coordinate and checked-arithmetic behavior remains in force.

knownLimitations: The current public Search SQL constructors remain two-argument and therefore retain sensitive, non-whole-word behavior; exposure through the later versioned request parser is outside this scope.
No native Search backend is advertised by this repository, so managed/native parity is not claimed for an unimplemented combination; unknown case values are rejected rather than silently downgraded.

Original-byte coordinates remain limited to the current strict file-backed UTF-8/UTF-16 reader; injected decoded TextReader sources expose null byte fields, and partial-surrogate literal spans are not assigned fabricated byte ranges.
The repository-wide suite retains 31 expected skips and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips; no package was published.
